propositions: The caused_by auto-derivation fallback lacks a provenance marker, making blamed edges indistinguishable from explicitly supplied ones on read, preventing metrics and consumers from weighing confidence differently.

On a population of 88 closed bugs carrying caused_by edges, the deriver reproduces 38 (43%), fails to reproduce 44 (50%), and contradicts 6 (7%); against 8 bugs with independently proven origins, it reproduces zero and confidently names the wrong actor in one case.

Defect shapes that dominate the codebase (unmet obligations, carrier commits, omissions) are structurally hard for file-level blame; the deriver's fail-closed majority rule (>50% threshold) abstains on 7 of 8 proven cases rather than guessing.

The confident-but-wrong case (consumer-edited-last, producer-innocent shape) is not preventable by shape detection because defect shape is not observable to the blame mechanism without semantic understanding of the code contract.

A derived vs explicit provenance marker on the link event would cost one field and make escape-rate lenses and epic-close metrics computable, enabling consumers to weight or exclude unverifiable attributions.

No schema change, deriver behaviour change, or review criterion should be implemented here; the provenance marker and any downstream metric adjustment are operator-adjudicated proposals filed as separate tickets.
